answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral: when k identities coordinate an equivocation, the protocol imposes a quadratic penalty O(k^2), rather than treating violations independently. Detection also applies an exponential multiplier to the swarm’s aggregate capital loss, while asymmetric depreciation reduces surviving collateral and blocks cheap re-entry. This remains effective for ferrous, harbor, or juniper-labeled nodes because aliases cannot dilute correlated evidence.
